hero.label: Services
hero.title: Design first. Drawings follow.
hero.intro: Five services, listed in the order a project uses them. Residential design leads. Construction documents come last, as the next step for design clients.

labels.credit: credit toward a full-service package booked within 14 days
labels.buildersLink: See how MDS works with builders

labels.guideLead: Not sure which professional your project needs? Read:

residential-design.what: This is the service for custom home design, house plans, and home additions. A designer works with you from the first sketch to a resolved design. Predesign sets the program, the code and zoning limits, and a first cost estimate. Schematic design then tests, usually, three options, and you choose one. Design development refines the chosen option. Design-only drawings are not permit-ready and are not for construction. A design client can continue into construction documents with MDS.
included: Predesign: site, code, and zoning review, and a program document
Preliminary cost estimate from the program
Schematic design, usually three options, with sketches and massing studies
Plans, elevations, and sections
Models and 3D views
Material and color palette exploration
Design development: refined plans, elevations, and sections, and material, finish, and fixture selection
Lighting and electrical concept plans
Two rounds of revisions in each phase
notIncluded: Construction documents, permit set, and permit submittal. These are the next step, below.
Structural, mechanical, electrical, or plumbing engineering
Surveys and soils tests. Predesign recommends them when they are needed.
deliverables: Schematic design set at 1/4 inch scale: floor plans and elevations
Design development package: plans, elevations, sections, and material selections
residential-design.suits: Owners building or changing a home who want design judgment, not only drawings.
residential-design.duration: About 9 to 15 weeks through design development: predesign takes 1 to 3 weeks, schematic design 4 to 6, and design development 4 to 6.

meta.title: Custom Home and Addition Design | Maneda Design Studios
meta.description: Custom home design, house plans and addition design: predesign, schematic design and design development. About 9 to 15 weeks, quoted after a conversation.

interior-design.what: Full-service interior design, from plans to furnishings. The work runs in four phases: discovery and concept, design and documentation, furniture and styling, and optional procurement and installation support. On full-scope residential projects, interiors can run alongside the building design, so the total is about 5 to 7 months, not the sum of both.
included: Client interview, site visit, and visual concept boards
Space plans and interior elevations for kitchen, bath, and millwork
Reflected ceiling plans with lighting layout
Material and finish schedules: tile, flooring, paint, and counters
Fixture and appliance selections, and a spec book for the contractor
Furniture plan by room, sourcing list, and budget tracker
Decor, window treatments, and light fixtures
Optional: procurement support, order coordination, and a final styling walkthrough
notIncluded: Construction, furnishings, and contractor costs. These are separate.
deliverables: Mood boards and a material inspiration sheet
CAD and PDF floor plans, reflected ceiling plans, and interior elevations
Install day checklist, if procurement support is chosen
interior-design.suits: Owners of new homes, renovations, and additions who want interiors resolved with the building, not added after it.
interior-design.duration: Typical length is 12 to 18 weeks. Under 1,500 SF takes 10 to 14 weeks, 1,500 to 2,500 SF takes 12 to 18, and 2,500 to 3,500 SF or more takes 16 to 24.

meta.title: Full-Service Interior Design | Maneda Design Studios
meta.description: Interior design from plans to furnishings, in four phases, run alongside the building design on full-scope residential projects. Quoted after a conversation.

site-analysis.what: A written report on a lot before you buy it or design on it. It sets out what zoning, setbacks, flood zone, and access allow, and what the lot can hold, using public records and a site visit. It is an informal zoning summary for design planning. It is not a survey, a legal opinion, or an engineering study. Final development rights must be confirmed by a licensed professional or the local building department.
included: Pre-visit research: zoning district, setbacks, lot coverage, height limits, and open space requirements
Aerial and GIS overlay analysis, and a basic flood zone check
Site visit of up to 1.5 hours, with photo documentation
Notes on access, driveway, drainage, views, sun path, noise, privacy, topography, and tree cover
Bubble diagrams and massing sketches
Opportunities and constraints narrative
Next step roadmap with suggested services
An optional layout concept
site-analysis.suits: Buyers comparing lots, owners planning an addition, and builders testing a site before committing.
site-analysis.duration: The site visit is 3 to 5 days after booking. The report follows 5 business days after the visit.

meta.title: Lot and Site Analysis Report | Maneda Design Studios
meta.description: A written report on what zoning, setbacks, flood zone and access allow on a lot, before you buy it or design on it. Two fixed prices by lot size.

consultations.what: A working session with a designer on a room or a set of rooms: layout, materials, color, furniture, and lighting. Choose a 1 hour video call, a 90 minute visit, or a 2 hour deep dive. You get a written follow-up, and a credit applies toward a full-service package booked within 14 days.
included: Virtual, 1 hour: live video call, with a room review from photos, videos, or floor plans you send in advance
In person, 90 minutes: walkthrough of up to 2 spaces, a measurement check, and a rough layout sketch if needed

Deep dive, 2 hours: full walkthrough and interview for up to 3 spaces, layout and space flow strategy, finish and material suggestions, furniture and lighting advice, and rough plan and elevation markups
notIncluded: A full design set or drawings for construction
deliverables: Virtual: follow-up email with a bullet summary within 24 hours
In person: summary email within 48 hours, and a rough layout sketch
Deep dive: one-page concept summary PDF within 3 business days, and a follow-up email with links and recommendations
consultations.suits: Homeowners who need direction before a full project, DIY clients, and owners preparing a room overhaul or a multi-room refresh.
consultations.duration: Written summary within 24 hours to 3 business days, depending on the session.

meta.title: Design Consultations | Maneda Design Studios
meta.description: A working session with a designer on layout, materials, color, furniture and lighting. Virtual or in person, with a written follow-up.

construction-documents.what: The next step after design. Once the design is approved, it is developed into a set of construction documents, so the design that was approved is the design that gets built. Construction documents take about 8 to 12 weeks. If you want, MDS continues with permit support, bidding support, and construction administration. This service is offered to design clients. Formal review, approval, and certification actions are performed by the licensed professional of record.
included: Construction drawings and specifications: plans, sections, elevations, and details
Interior and exterior details
Coordination with structural, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing consultants
Permit set preparation, permit submittal and tracking, and responses to review comments
Optional: bid packages, pre-bid meetings, and review of bids
Optional: construction administration with site visits, requests for information, submittal tracking, and punch list review
notIncluded: Structural engineering. The owner hires a structural engineer under a separate contract.
deliverables: Closeout documents, if construction administration is chosen
construction-documents.suits: Design clients whose approved design is ready to be priced, permitted, and built.
construction-documents.duration: Construction documents take 8 to 12 weeks. Permitting takes 3 to 8 weeks, depending on the jurisdiction. Bidding takes 2 to 4 weeks. Construction administration lasts as long as construction.

meta.title: Construction Documents for Homes | Maneda Design Studios
meta.description: Construction documents and permit drawings for homes and additions, developed from the approved design in about 8 to 12 weeks, with permit support if you want it.

items: No stamped or sealed drawings by MDS

builders.label: Builders and developers
builders.title: Design partner for builders and developers.
builders.text: Bring MDS in at the design stage, so the project is resolved before it is priced and built. Early design decisions are cheaper to change than built ones. You can take design only, schematic design and design development, and hand it to the professional of your choice for construction documents. Or continue with MDS into construction documents.

terms.label: Terms
terms.title: How engagements work.
items: Every engagement is confirmed in writing before work begins.
Each project gets a written fixed fee at the proposal stage, set by phase, so the cost is known before work starts.
Each phase fee is invoiced in two parts: half to start the phase and half on delivery. Invoices are due within 7 days, and the next phase starts when the invoice is paid.
Two rounds of revisions are included in each phase. Added rounds are billed at an hourly rate.
The schedule pauses while the project waits on your approvals or information. Durations assume approvals within 5 business days.

Fees cover design services only. Construction, permit fees, furnishings, contractor costs, and engineering are separate. Engineers and other consultants are hired and paid by the owner under separate contracts.
Zoning and code summaries are informal and are not legal opinions.
Consultation and site visit credits apply to a full-service package booked within 14 days. Credits cannot be transferred.

meta.title: Home Design Process and Timeline | Maneda Design Studios
meta.description: How a residential design project works with MDS, from inquiry to construction documents, with what happens, what you provide, and what you get.

hero.label: Process
hero.title: How a project works.
hero.intro: Six phases, in plain language. Most of the value sits in phases four and five, where the design is decided.

phases.title: Inquiry and scope
phases.happens: You send the inquiry form. We review it and reply, and we talk through the project, the lot, and the budget range.
phases.provide: Project description, site location, target start, and files or photos if you have them.
phases.get: A clear read on fit, and the next step.
phases.duration: Reply within 1 business day. Scoping call within 3 business days.

phases.title: Proposal and agreement
phases.happens: We send a written proposal with scope, deliverables, and fee. You review it and sign the agreement.
phases.provide: Questions, decisions, and the signed agreement.
phases.get: A written scope, a deliverables list, and a fee.
phases.duration: Written proposal within 5 business days of the call. The schedule starts when the agreement is signed.

phases.title: Site and code review
phases.happens: We review the lot, zoning, setbacks, flood zone, and the jurisdiction's rules. Constraints are found before they shape the design. We also recommend added pre-work when it is needed, such as a survey or soils tests.
phases.provide: Survey, plat, or deed if you have them. Site access if a visit is needed.
phases.get: A constraints summary that frames the design.

phases.title: Concept and schematic design
phases.happens: We develop, usually, three options with sketches, plans, elevations, and massing studies. Each option shows how the house sits, how light enters, and how the rooms connect. You choose one.
phases.provide: Feedback on the options. Your priorities for rooms, light, and budget.
phases.get: Concept sketches, massing and plan studies, 3D views, and a schematic design set.

phases.title: Design development and revisions
phases.happens: The chosen design is resolved: room sizes, openings, materials, and finishes. Revisions are made in the rounds defined in the agreement.
phases.provide: Decisions on materials and finishes, and timely feedback.
phases.get: A design development set and material and finish direction.

phases.title: Construction documents and permit support
phases.happens: For design clients, the approved design is developed into construction documents and coordinated for permit submittal. The set goes to your builder as the basis for pricing and construction. Structural drawings are prepared by a structural engineer, hired by the owner under a separate contract.
phases.provide: Your builder and engineers, if you have them. Responses to permit review comments.
phases.get: A construction document set and support through permit review comments.
phases.duration: Construction documents 8 to 12 weeks, then permitting 3 to 8 weeks, depending on the jurisdiction

sketch.label: Sketch to finished drawing
sketch.title: From the first idea to the final sheet.

items.q: How long does a permit take?
items.a: Permitting typically takes 3 to 8 weeks, depending on the jurisdiction. The jurisdiction sets the review time, not the studio.

Where a seal is required, drawings are reviewed and sealed by a licensed professional of record. On residential projects this is often the structural engineer, hired and paid by the owner under a separate contract. MDS coordinates the drawings with the engineer during construction documents. Where a jurisdiction requires a different professional, MDS confirms that during site and code review.
Two rounds of revisions are included in each phase. Added rounds are billed at an hourly rate.

items.q: What file formats do I receive?
items.a: PDF for review and permit submittal. Interior packages include CAD and PDF floor plans. Native Revit files are not shared.

Each project gets a written fixed fee at the proposal stage, set by phase, so the cost is known before work starts. Each phase fee is invoiced in two parts: half to start the phase and half on delivery. The next phase starts when the invoice is paid. Invoices are due within 7 days. Consultations, site analysis reports, and site visits are paid in advance.

Based in Orlando, Florida. Projects across the United States. At the start of every project, MDS researches the jurisdiction: which code applies, size and height limits, seal and engineering triggers, and the submittal format.
Yes. Meetings and design review are held in English or Portuguese, as you prefer. Drawings submitted to jurisdictions are in English.

items.q: What do you need from me to start?
items.a: A project description, the site address or parcel, any survey or existing plans, photos, a budget range, and a target start. The inquiry form asks for these.

MDS does not build or run a construction site. Construction administration is offered as an option: site visits, requests for information, submittal tracking, and punch list review. Formal review, approval, and certification actions are performed by the licensed professional of record.
MDS is a design studio. Requests for drawings only are reviewed case by case through the contact form.

process.durationNote: Durations assume a single-family residence of about 2,000 to 3,500 SF and your approvals within 5 business days. Predesign through construction documents takes 16 to 24 weeks. Commercial and retail projects add 30 to 50 percent for engineer and tenant coordination.

meta.title: Residential Designer in Orlando | Maneda Design Studios
meta.description: Manolo Castaneda, residential designer. 10+ years in multifamily and retail projects. Based in Orlando, Florida. Bilingual in English and Portuguese.

hero.label: About
hero.title: Manolo Castaneda
hero.portraitAlt: Portrait of Manolo Castaneda, Residential Designer.

story: Manolo Castaneda is a residential designer with more than 10 years of experience in multifamily and retail projects. He trained in architecture in Brazil and the United States, with degrees from the Catholic University of Brasilia and NJIT. He is bilingual in English and Brazilian Portuguese and is based in Orlando, Florida.

He designs from the site and from how people live in a building: space, light, circulation, and how a room is used. A design is not finished until it can be permitted and built, so local code and jurisdiction rules are part of the process from the first sketch. Code literacy is what lets a design get built. It is part of the work, not a separate service.

values.label: What I value
values.title: What I value in a project.
items: Start with the site. The lot and the way the owners live decide more than the style does.
Test the idea against how the room is used. If it looks good and works badly, I drop it.
Say why. Every decision has a reason I can explain to the owner and to the builder.

privacy.title: Privacy policy

sections.title: What we collect
sections.text: When you send an inquiry, we receive what you type in the form: name, email, optional phone, project details, and any file link you share. We use it only to reply to you and to scope your project.

sections.title: How the form works
